New Waze Alert Now Live, Powered by Garmin Watches: Everything You Need To Know
10 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution/Garmin
What was only a rumor one week ago is now official, as Garmin and Waze have confirmed a new partnership supposed to increase awareness for cyclists on the road.
Thanks to this collaboration, Waze will begin showing notifications in the places where cyclists are expected to be on the road, thanks to location data provided by Garmin Edge bike computers and Garmin smartwatches.
In other words, if you’re a cyclist and want to make sure that drivers know you’re there, you can configure your Garmin devices to send your location to the Waze app. Nearby drivers will receive a notification in the navigation app, so they can slow down before they reach the location where you’re flagged.
Here’s everything you need to know about this feature.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution How it works Garmin devices can already know where you are once you enable LiveTrack. This is a safety feature that users can enable to share their real-time location with selected contacts whenever they start an outdoor activity.
Users can let these contacts see their location on the map, with the data being broadcast through the smartphone (via the Garmin Connect app), on a live web link.
In addition to the current location, LiveTrack also shares additional information regarding the workout, such as the average pace, the elapsed time of the activity, the distance traveled, and the heart rate.
While most devices share the location data after they acquire the GPS signal through the Garmin Connect app using Bluetooth, some smartwatches also feature LTE support and can share the location data directly through the LTE connection, without using Bluetooth. These devices include the Fenix 9 Pro, the Forerunner 945 LTE, the quatix 8 Pro, the fenix 8 Pro with AMOLED and microLED, and the D2 Mach 2 Pro.
However, Waze users will only see the location of the cyclist on the map, without additional information being imported. Furthermore, no personal details are revealed, so the only thing that’s displayed is a cyclist icon in the place where the Garmin device was located and a notification on the screen reading “Cyclist ahead.”
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution The supported devices Garmin does not provide and maintain a list of devices that support LiveTrack, but the company specifically mentions EDGE bike computers and smartwatches as being compatible with the new Waze feature.
Theoretically, all Fenix models that are still being serviced should be able to work with LiveTrack, as well as Instinct smartwatches and the luxury models in the Marq lineup. If you’re not sure if LiveTrack is available for your device, the easiest way to figure this out is to open the Garmin Connect app, tap the More icon in the bottom-right corner, and expand the Safety & Tracking section.
If LiveTrack is there, this means that your device should be able to share your location while cycling, assuming you have already configured this feature.
As for Waze, you need to be running the latest version of the app on Android or iPhone. Android Auto and CarPlay are also supported, but at this point, there’s no word as to whether Garmin and Waze want to bring the same information to cars with Google built-in.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution How to set up the feature If you ride your bike on public roads regularly and you already own a compatible Garmin device, you need to configure LiveTrack to share the location data with Waze.
To do this, you must install the latest version of the Garmin Connect app from your app store - LiveTrack requires at least version 5.20.
Once you are there, you must open the app and tap the More button in the lower part of the screen. Look for Safety & Tracking and tap LiveTrack. Follow the wizard on the screen to complete the setup - you’ll be prompted to define the contacts you want to allow to track you and configure how notifications will be sent. For text messages, you’ll need to pay for a Garmin Connect+ subscription.
When everything is complete, you should see a new section called Waze Location Sharing. You’ll also need to set up this feature, but the wizard shouldn’t require more than a couple of seconds to complete. Once this feature is enabled, drivers should start to see your location on the map when you start cycling on a public road, acquire a GPS signal, and activate LiveTrack.
Keep in mind that you’ll need to have your phone in your pocket or backpack (unless your Garmin device is fitted with LTE) and have a good cellular signal to be able to share your location in real time. The location data is automatically removed when you end the workout, so you will no longer be visible on Waze.
Google insists on the privacy part of the feature, explaining sharing the data with Waze is “completely opt-in and built with privacy in mind.” The company explains that the alert appearing on Waze screens is just temporary.
